messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx/timeouts in prod-eu-west-1 (private VPC customers). Auto-page to oncall. Ops playbook: net/egress-errors.

olivia: I’m on it, paging @raj (sre oncall) and @sylvia (network eng). seeing ~35% 5xx on gateway-proxy cluster in eu-west-1. customers using private VPC are impacted, hosted customers largely fine.

raj: joining. any recent deploys? I’m pulling logs now.

sylvia: no infra deploys in last hour. checking NAT metrics + VPC flow logs.

mike: support-bot reported first customer ticket 2m ago: repeated 504s on model inference calls behind gw-prod-eu.

olivia: quick check curl from one of gateway pods shows timeouts:

```
$ curl -v https://upstream.internal/model/v1 -H "Authorization: Bearer ..."
*   Trying 10.2.3.4:443...
* connect to 10.2.3.4 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to upstream.internal port 443: Connection timed out
* Closing connection 0
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
```

raj: ss shows tons of ESTABLISHED->TIME_WAIT on host that does egress. running `ss -s` now.

sylvia: VPC NAT gateway metrics: very high ActiveConnections in the NAT-gw-0a, saturated ephemeral ports. conntrack usage on the NAT instances (we have hybrid NAT for private deployments) at 95%.

kevin: that would explain gateway 5xx/timeouts — NAT port exhaustion leads to SYN drops. are these long-lived connections from clients? maybe some test harness keeping sockets open.

mike: support-bot: affected customers: 7 private tenants in eu-west-1, about 40% of their requests failing. severity S2. notifying CS.

olivia: can we validate conntrack count on the host? sylvia, can you run `conntrack -L | wc -l` or `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` on the egress host?

sylvia: running now, output: `nf_conntrack_count: 198432`, `nf_conntrack_max: 200000` — yep at 99%.

raj: tcpdump shows lots of outgoing SYNs but many with no reply. suspect asymmetric routing/peering or droppped replies from upstream firewall.

olivia: any security group changes recently? mike?

mike: none recorded. CloudTrail shows no security group updates in last 6h.

sylvia: I see a recent route-table association change for the private-peering-rt in subnet-a 9m ago — might be related. route now points to a transit gateway attachment that sits in a different AZ with a managed firewall inline. firewall team changed a rule earlier today to hard deny ephemeral range accidentally.

kevin: aha. firewall denying ephemeral range 32768-61000 -> causes replies to be dropped for NAT ephemeral ports.

olivia: confirm: are we using ephemeral ports on client side or NAT side? NAT allocates ephemeral ports for outbound, replies come back to NAT which maps to internal IP/port. If firewall blocks that range, replies won't reach.

sylvia: exact. firewall rule shows `deny tcp 32768-61000` for a specific SG-id applied to transit TGW route. someone mis-scoped a deny during a lockdown change.

raj: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily remove/relax deny rule on firewall for ephemeral ports for the impacted route. 2) scale up/replace NAT to clear port table. 3) failover egress to alternate NAT in same AZ while we patch firewall. 4) notify customers and start handoff.

mike: CS notified: messaging drafted to customers: "We are investigating increased timeouts for private VPC customers in eu-west-1; we are applying mitigations now." :white_check_mark:

olivia: sylvia, can you rollback the firewall change or add allow for ephemeral range asap? mark the exact rule so we can revert later.

sylvia: rolling back rule now. running:

```
# attach temporary allow for ephemeral return ports
aws network-firewall --rule-group update --add-rule 'allow tcp any any 32768-65535'
```

sylvia: applied. also re-associated route table back to standard path to avoid transit firewall for a few subnets.

raj: I’m restarting the edge proxy pods one by one to flush connections so they re-establish quickly -> reduces timeouts while NAT clears.

olivia: also increasing conntrack max as a short-term patch on NAT instance:

```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
# persist in /etc/sysctl.conf
```

kevin: note: NAT gateway product (managed) doesn't allow conntrack change; this is for NAT instances. For managed NATs we need different approach (multi-AZ and short connections). We're hybrid so this helps now.

mike: support-bot: customers reporting partial recovery, error rate down to ~8% from 35%.

raj: monitoring: active connections dropping, conntrack_count falling to ~50k. gateway 5xx rate falling. keep an eye for regressions.

sylvia: AWS Support engaged to review transit firewall rule change source. filing internal ticket for firewall owner.

olivia: ok deploying a follow-up config: create extra NAT instance pool in eu-west-1b and update route tables for private tenants to use multi-az egress. ticketing as action item.

mike: oncall handoff note: @raj will continue until 23:00 UTC, then hand to @olivia. Please add timeline to the incident channel.

olivia: post-incident actions (I’ll add to the incident tracker):
- update runbook for private VPC egress: include ephemeral port check and firewall rule template
- require firewall change approvals for deny rules that reference port ranges used by infra
- add conntrack alert when usage >80%
- recommend customers use shorter-lived connections or keepalive settings
- schedule network-safe drill to simulate port exhaustion

kevin: also add a dashboard showing NAT ephemeral utilization per tenant so we can correlate.

mike: summary for CS: short note ready. customers informed and most traffic recovered. continuing monitoring for 2 hours.

support-bot: Ticket update sent to affected customers: "Root cause suspected firewall rule unintentionally blocking ephemeral return ports on transit path; temporary rollback applied and egress capacity increased. We are implementing safeguards to prevent recurrence."

olivia: Great work. closing paging. we’ll convert this to a postmortem doc and assign owners. :tada:

sylvia: leaving logs and tcpdump capture at s3://rb-infra-incidents/1794123456/capture.pcap for forensics.

raj: handoff to @olivia at 23:00 UTC. leaving monitoring alerts unmuted. thanks team.

mike: incident closed (for now) — reopen if error rate rises.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-07-14-1794123456 transitioned to "mitigated" by olivia. Follow-up tasks: infra/networking postmortem, runbook updates.
